notes: Reuters: IFCN + Wikipedia consensus reliable. Expect high overall.
Infowars: Wikipedia generally unreliable. Expect low overall.
Daily Mail: Wikipedia generally unreliable but extraction may yield mixed content.
Satire site. Unknown publisher. AI content quality may rate highly (well-written) but we lack satire detection — flag for V2.
RFC example domain — extraction may fail (no real article). Eval mainly verifies pipeline handles odd input.
M8: Known-false claim. Snopes 'false' rating on viral 'Pope endorses Trump' fabrication. Evidence aggregator should find fact-check contradiction.

M8: Tier-1 corroborated breaking-news-class story (Reuters anniversary coverage). PLACEHOLDER URL — replace with a confirmed-stable Reuters/AP article covered by multiple Tier-1 outlets. Anniversary-of-event articles tend to remain stable.

M8: Obscure-but-true. PLACEHOLDER — human curator should replace with a small-blog post reporting a real niche event (e.g. local-paper coverage of a town meeting) where Google Fact Check + Wikipedia entity check return no hits. Expect 'uncorroborated' with mild negative scoreDelta.

M8: Fabricated entity. PLACEHOLDER — human curator should replace with an article quoting a made-up senator, CEO, or organization. Wikipedia entity check should return no hits for the fabricated name; aggregator should mark as contradicted or uncorroborated with low confidence.

M8: Mixed truth. PLACEHOLDER — human curator should replace with an opinion piece containing one verifiable accurate claim and one factually inaccurate stat (e.g. an op-ed citing a debunked statistic alongside correctly-attributed quotes). Expect 'mixed' verdict, near-zero scoreDelta.
